title: Keep the Android application portrait-only
environment: Android app; user reports that the landscape layout does not work well. Specific affected controls and device states have not been recorded.
reproduction_status: Sensor-driven regression reproduces landscape launch on the original APK after a passing Settings rotation control. With the portrait manifest, all 11 orientation/state checks and 18 updated popup checks pass on the API 36 phone emulator. The user waived physical Android 17 phone testing and requested the commit; physical-phone verification was not performed.
reproduction: Open QShopper on Android with system auto-rotation enabled.
Observe the landscape usability problems reported by the user; capture specific layout or interaction failures when implementing the ticket.
actual: The application allows landscape orientation, which the user reports does not work well.
expected: The Android application remains in portrait orientation, supporting the intended one-handed shopping experience.
source_notes: The activity previously used android:screenOrientation="unspecified"; it now requests "portrait".
Record the portrait-only requirement rather than redesigning the landscape interface.
Verify the manifest request on supported Android versions and device/window configurations when implementing; a manifest value alone is not proof of actual orientation behavior.

During UI-010 verification on 2026-10-29, the native pull-to-edit stroke did not reliably activate editing in the short landscape viewport. Popup tests enter edit mode in portrait before rotating, and assert actual display/accessibility rotation. This is an observed example supporting the existing landscape-usability report; no landscape redesign is selected.

Android 16/API 36 can ignore orientation restrictions on displays at least sw600dp for apps targeting API 36. The temporary large-screen opt-out stops applying when targeting API 37. Record this OS limitation rather than adding an unreliable runtime orientation workaround.
acceptance_criteria: Launching the Android app while the phone is held in portrait or landscape presents the app in portrait.
Rotating the phone with system auto-rotation enabled keeps the app in portrait in shopping and edit modes, including with the drawer or keyboard open.
The orientation restriction preserves list contents, ordering, checked state and text being edited.
Add automated Android regression coverage that fails before the orientation restriction and passes afterward; verify actual activity orientation rather than only inspecting the manifest.
Confirm the intended behavior on the physical Android phone and document any platform-specific limits.
evidence: User backlog request on 2026-10-29: application should be portrait-only because landscape does not work well; suggested setting this in the Android manifest.

implementation.change: Request portrait orientation on QtActivity in the Android manifest. No runtime orientation handler is needed.

regression.before: The sensor control rotates Android Settings to 3120x1440, rotation 1. The original QShopper APK also launches at 3120x1440 while held landscape, failing launch_held_landscape.
regression.coverage: Auto-rotate enabled with real emulated acceleration sensors, cold launches held portrait/landscape, shopping rotation in both directions, edit mode with keyboard closed/open, retained unfinished text, drawer state, process continuity, saved item order and checked state. Verify actual display geometry before and after accessibility inspection. Restore acceleration and rotation settings afterward.
regression.after: All 11 checks pass. The Settings control rotates to landscape; QShopper remains 1440x3120, rotation 0, with auto-rotate enabled and sensor-driven rotation attempts. Draft text, IME/drawer state, process, saved order and checked flags are preserved.

implementation.existing_tests: Update the UI-010 popup matrix from true landscape to a rotated-device request while the phone app remains portrait. The earlier UI-010 landscape results remain valid historical evidence for that earlier build.
implementation.platform_limit: The manifest request is verified on the API 36 phone emulator (sw411dp). Large-screen overrides (sw600dp or larger), multi-window behavior and OEM/user overrides are not universally prevented by a manifest orientation request.
implementation.remaining: None for UI-011. The user waived physical-phone testing and accepted automated verification. Android large-screen/windowing/user overrides remain documented platform limits.
verification: Windows configure/build and all three CTest entries pass: 85 UI, 6 keyboard and 52 model records. Log: out/windows-agent/tests/ui011-verify.txt.
Native portrait/state regression: 11 checks pass in out/android-emulator/ui011-after/results.json.
Updated native selector regression with rotated-device request: 18 checks pass in out/android-emulator/ui011-popups-after/results.json.
x86_64 and ARM64 APKs rebuilt. ARM64 APK signature verified with shared-key SHA-256 7c4335c93ec24cb0f92b44ae84ce108180cb299b43ea4e6ef5baafaef7ae029b.
implementation.phone_validation: Waived by the user on 2026-10-29: "no need to test on phone. Commit the change". No physical-device installation or verification was performed.

acceptance_notes: The physical-phone acceptance check was explicitly waived by the user. Automated sensor-driven before/after regression coverage and updated popup checks pass; platform-specific limits are documented.
